# The support you deserve from an ally you can trust.

Alliance is your guide to health care services that help you live your best life.

[ Get Started ][47]

## Healthcare doesn't have to be complicated.

Alliance is proud to offer a comprehensive list of services for every age and ability to simplify
the process of finding and coordinating the varying supports you need.

### CFSS Support

 Flexible, self-directed options to meet your needs.

[ Learn more ][48]

### Consultation Services

Helping you understand the new CFSS program.

[ Learn more ][49]

### Financial Management

Flexibility and control to customize your care.

[ Learn more ][50]

### 245D Licensed Support

Individualized support in your home and community.

[ Learn more ][51]

### Mental Health

A variety of support services and therapy to help you flourish.

[ Learn more ][52]

### Medical Supply

Find equipment and supplies tailored to your needs.

[ Learn more ][53]

### Home Health

Care for your everyday needs in the comfort of your home.

[ Learn more ][54]

## Alliance Health Care builds bridges between people and the services they need.

Healthcare options can be a confusing maze that keeps people from finding the services and supports
they need. We believe something as essential as healthcare shouldn’t be hard, which is why we bring
together a thorough knowledge of the healthcare system and comprehensive services to deliver
high-quality individualized care.

Person-Centered

We recognize the inherent worth of every human being. Therefore, we believe that quality healthcare
is each person’s right, no matter who they are or what support they need. We build options that
start with the kind of life each person wants to live, and tailor our service delivery to meet those
desires.

Accessibility

Removing barriers and providing equal access to healthcare is an essential mission of Alliance.  We
offer our comprehensive list of services in all communities and strive to support your needs, no
matter how complex or varied they might be. 

Competence

Alliance started when our owner needed support at home for her daughter with Down Syndrome.  Our
personal experience, coupled with over three decades in the healthcare industry, gives us a unique
combination of both empathy and expertise.  We keep your perspective in mind when working with you
to provide personalized services that make sense for your life. 

Advocacy

Alliance is involved in many community and state initiatives to develop best practices and advocate
for increased support to the aging, disability, and mental health communities.  We listen to our
clients' individual needs and preferences and connect them to available resources, services, and
supports.

Inclusion

"We're the same. We're different. That's what makes the world such fun." ~ Sesame Street

Alliance recognizes and honors the uniqueness of every individual. We foster a culture of
inclusivity by providing healthcare services and employment opportunities that respects the needs
and preferences of each person’s culture, class, age, ability, and socioeconomic background, without
discrimination. 

[ Get Started ][55]

## Let's keep things simple.

Alliance is your guide to finding the right care that works for you. 

When you partner with Alliance, we strive to handle all of your healthcare needs, no matter how
complex or varied they might be.

[ Get Started ][56]

[Have a question?][57]

Alliance offers CFSS, Consultation Services, Financial Management (FMS), Mental Health, 245D
Licensed Support, Medical Supply, and Home Health services throughout the state of Minnesota.

# We are now Cencora. Our shared identity unites us.

Cencora brings the companies and services of AmerisourceBergen together under one new name.

[ Meet Cencora ][86]
[A banner that says We Are Cencora on a pink and purple background]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]
[GettyImages-907614352_JPG]

## In the news

Read the latest press releases and media mentions.
[ Explore newsroom ][92]

## Insights

Access the newest in thought leadership.
[ Explore insights ][93]

# Careers with purpose

With a global presence and 44,000+ team members strong, AmerisourceBergen is committed to making a
difference in the future of health.
[ Explore careers ][94]
[GettyImages-1178

# Building a world of health around every individual

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

# Building a world of health around every individual

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

## Celerion’s commitment to swift, exceptional research through translational medicine.

Every day, we use our experience, agility, and innovative research strategies to help get your drug
to market faster—so your treatments can touch the lives of family, friends, and people in need
around the world.

## What We Do

Celerion accelerates drug development through world-class early-phase clinical research and advanced
bioanalysis services. We conduct early-phase clinical studies and provide bioanalytical support
across all stages of development, from preclinical through late-stage clinical. Our clinical and
bioanalytical teams draw on deep global expertise to deliver fast, reliable data and insights that
support confident decision-making.

[Learn More][139]

## Early Phase Clinical Services

### Delivering Early Phase Confidence Through Expertise and Experience

With 50+ years of experience and more than 650 beds worldwide, we offer the largest global network
of early phase operations in the industry. Find out how our expertise, facilities, and full range of
clinical research services prepare us to address the unique needs of your product’s early phase
development.

[All Early Phase Clinical Services][140]

BIOANALYTICAL SCIENCE SPOTLIGHT

## At the Speed of Science

Celerion’s bioanalytical laboratories in Lincoln, NE and Zurich, Switzerland are equipped with the
latest technologies for PK, immunogenicity, and biomarker assays to provide regulated support at all
phases of drug development.

[Learn More][147]

## Bioanalytical Sciences

For over 40 years, Celerion’s bioanalytical laboratories have provided end-to-end support for drug
developers from pre-clinical through late-stage clinical testing. Learn how our experienced
scientific teams can provide custom, phase-appropriate bioanalytical solutions for your program.

[Bioanalytical Sciences Overview][148]

CLINICAL RESEARCH SPOTLIGHT

## The Future of Pharmacy

We’ve got our eyes set on the future. We’re taking research higher, discoveries further, and
translating science into medicine day by day.

[Learn More][155]

## Therapeutic Expertise Areas

### Focused on Strong Science and Flawless Execution

Between our comprehensive services and decades of therapeutic experience, we have the expertise to
handle every aspect of your product’s early development—no matter the type of drug or clinical
trial. These are some of the many specialties we’ve cultivated over the years, to provide fast,
innovative solutions for your drug’s development.

## What Sets Us Apart

[AGILE ICON][AGILE ICON]

#### AGILE

Speed is part of our name. We optimize our studies for speed and efficiency at every stage, to
generate actionable data faster than our competitors.

[EXPERIENCED ICON][EXPERIENCED ICON]

#### EXPERIENCED

Our 50+ years of experience conducting 6,000+ studies ensures the collection of quality data through
efficient and effective study designs.

[GLOBAL ICON][GLOBAL ICON]

#### GLOBAL

With facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia, in 30 countries worldwide, we conduct trials
with the right patients, in the right places, to get the data you need.

[INNOVATIVE ICON][INNOVATIVE ICON]

#### INNOVATIVE

From data acquisition strategies to advanced facilities, we lead the way in leveraging new
technology to provide faster, more accurate data, at less cost.

## Celerion’s commitment to swift, exceptional research through translational medicine.

Every day, we use our experience, agility, and innovative research strategies to help get your drug
to market faster—so your treatments can touch the lives of family, friends, and people in need
around the world.

## What We Do

Celerion accelerates drug development through world-class early-phase clinical research and advanced
bioanalysis services. We conduct early-phase clinical studies and provide bioanalytical support
across all stages of development, from preclinical through late-stage clinical. Our clinical and
bioanalytical teams draw on deep global expertise to deliver fast, reliable data and insights that
support confident decision-making.

[Learn More][139]

## Early Phase Clinical Services

### Delivering Early Phase Confidence Through Expertise and Experience

With 50+ years of experience and more than 650 beds worldwide, we offer the largest global network
of early phase operations in the industry. Find out how our expertise, facilities, and full range of
clinical research services prepare us to address the unique needs of your product’s early phase
development.

phases of drug development.

## Bioanalytical Sciences

For over 40 years, Celerion’s bioanalytical laboratories have provided end-to-end support for drug
developers from pre-clinical through late-stage clinical testing. Learn how our experienced
scientific teams can provide custom, phase-appropriate bioanalytical solutions for your program.

Between our comprehensive services and decades of therapeutic experience, we have the expertise to

[

### Vision

We strive to transform Fresenius Kabi in the decade to come. We are committed to increase
efficiencies in the therapy and care of patients and improve access to high-quality healthcare
around the globe.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][107]
[

### Excellence

We are specialized in lifesaving medicines and technologies for critically and chronically ill
patients. With our passion and expertise, we touch the lives of almost 450 million people every
year, each one representing the importance of our work.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][108]
[

### Sustainability

We constantly strive to improve our sustainability footprint. For us, meeting the needs of patients
and healthcare professionals goes hand in hand with responsible and ethical management.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

[ Learn More ][126]

### [ Consumer Products & Services ][132]

Strengthening Healthcare
 

## Powering Care Locally

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting
providers, enabling access to medicines and therapies, and removing barriers across the patient
journey.

### Convenient. Reliable. Ships free.

Get your medications using Optum® Home Delivery and enjoy benefits like free standard shipping, 24/7
pharmacist access and more.

[Learn more][18]

### Expecting a delivery?

Eligible members can use our quick order tracker to see the status of your medication without
signing in.

[Track your order][19]

Optum now offers low-cost insulin for $35 a month for those without insurance.

Sign up

### Our promises

### Affordable

Get the medication you need, when you need it — your way.

options for you.

[Roche publishes its first quarter results for 2026][103]

Roche reports 7% (CER) sales for the full year results in 2025. Commenting on the results, CEO
Thomas Schinecker said: “2025 was a strong year for Roche, reflecting our continued focus on
operational and R&D excellence.”

the highlights in our Annual Report.

Our strategy

curative medicines.

## We are Roche

We combine life-changing diagnostics and medicines to take on the toughest healthcare challenges,
those that place the greatest strain on patients, families, communities, and health systems. 

Guided by the experiences of patients, we are determined to prevent, stop and cure diseases so
people can live healthier, longer lives.

[Man holding a surfing board smiling with a ocean in the background.]

## **An AASLD Membership Pays Off at The Liver Meeting®** 

Save up to $935 on The Liver Meeting when you join or renew today and *ELEVATE* your experience as a
member this November in Denver, Colorado. From the AASLD Member Lounge, Members’ Reception at the
Denver Art Museum, and preferred rates at Headquarter hotels, becoming a member today makes a
difference for your arrival in November.  

[Activate My Savings][80]

### 2027 AASLD Committee & SIG Nominations

Whether you're looking to grow professionally, give back to our community, or expand your network,
this is your chance to strengthen AASLD and the future of liver health. Put your skills and
expertise to work in the volunteer role where you can make the greatest impact. 

[Peer-nominate or self-nominate by July 30.][81]

### Now Live: The Liver Meeting® 2026 Preliminary Guide

Start planning your TLM26 journey with this sneak peek program filled with registration rates,
highly anticipated sessions like the Postgraduate Course and Basic Science Symposium, and tips to
help you prepare for this year’s meeting. Inside, find all the critical details like hotels to stay
at in Denver, Colorado, registration opening dates, and when late-breaking abstract applications
will be accepted. And don’t forget, TLM26 will start on a Thursday this year, so start getting ready
today!  

[Access the Guide Now][82]

### AASLD Foundation Awards Over $2 Million in Grants for 2026

This investment fuels innovative research to advance the understanding, prevention, diagnosis, and
treatment of liver disease, while also expanding access to trained hepatology providers and
strengthening the global community of investigators working toward cures. 

[Learn more.][83]

## Practice Guidelines

Stay on top of the latest recommendations for preferred approaches to diagnostic, therapeutic, and
preventative aspects of liver disease care. Developed by panels of experts, our guidelines are your
key resource for expert treatment.

[View Practice Guidelines][84]

Your donation helps us support people of all ages affected by any type of liver condition, provide

[Donate now][54]

**More about us**

### FAQs

###### Why did you change your name and rebrand as Liver UK?

Following our merger with Children’s Liver Disease Foundation, we created Liver UK to bring
everything together under one clear, inclusive identity and better reflect our role as the UK’s
liver health charity. [Read more.][55]

###### Do you support children and families?

Yes. Liver disease can affect people of all ages, including babies, children and young people. We
provide information and support for children, parents, carers and families, helping you understand
liver conditions and find the guidance you [need][56].

###### Do you support people with liver cancer?

Yes. Through Liver Cancer UK, we support people affected by liver cancer, including those who have
been diagnosed, people waiting for tests or treatment, and family members or carers. We can help you
find trusted information, understand what questions to ask, and feel less alone at each stage.  Find
out more by visiting [Liver Cancer UK][57].

###### How can I support Liver UK?

There are lots of ways to support our work. You can make a donation, fundraise, volunteer, leave a
gift in your will, support a campaign or help raise awareness by sharing your story. Every act of
support helps us be there for more people affected by liver disease and liver cancer. [Find out
more][58].

###### What are the signs and symptoms of liver disease?

Many liver conditions have no symptoms in the early stages, but signs can include fatigue, jaundice,
abdominal swelling and unexplained weight loss. It’s important to understand [the risk factors and
get tested][59] if you are worried.

###### Can liver disease be prevented?

Around 90% of liver disease in adults is considered preventable, with major risk factors including
alcohol harm, type 2 diabetes, obesity and viral hepatitis. Some liver diseases are caused by
genetic or autoimmune conditions.  You can find out more about [the risk factors here.][60]

**More about us**

### FAQs

###### Why did you change your name and rebrand as Liver UK?

Following our merger with Children’s Liver Disease Foundation, we created Liver UK to bring
everything together under one clear, inclusive identity and better reflect our role as the UK’s
liver health charity. [Read more.][55]

###### Do you support children and families?

Yes. Liver disease can affect people of all ages, including babies, children and young people. We
provide information and support for children, parents, carers and families, helping you understand
liver conditions and find the guidance you [need][56].

###### Do you support people with liver cancer?

Yes. Through Liver Cancer UK, we support people affected by liver cancer, including those who have
been diagnosed, people waiting for tests or treatment, and family members or carers. We can help you
find trusted information, understand what questions to ask, and feel less alone at each stage.  Find
out more by visiting [Liver Cancer UK][57].

###### How can I support Liver UK?

There are lots of ways to support our work. You can make a donation, fundraise, volunteer, leave a
gift in your will, support a campaign or help raise awareness by sharing your story. Every act of
support helps us be there for more people affected by liver disease and liver cancer. [Find out
more][58].

###### What are the signs and symptoms of liver disease?

Many liver conditions have no symptoms in the early stages, but signs can include fatigue, jaundice,
abdominal swelling and unexplained weight loss. It’s important to understand [the risk factors and
get tested][59] if you are worried.

###### Can liver disease be prevented?

Around 90% of liver disease in adults is considered preventable, with major risk factors including
alcohol harm, type 2 diabetes, obesity and viral hepatitis. Some liver diseases are caused by
genetic or autoimmune conditions.  You can find out more about [the risk factors here.][60]

# Gastroenterologists**

[Our Locations][12] [Book Appointment][13]

## About Continuum Gastroenterology Care

Located in the heart of Union County, we combine state-of-the-art technology with gentle care to
provide patients with the best digestive health and endoscopy services possible. We understand that
you need experienced gastroenterologist(s) you can trust. As leading gastroenterologists in Union
County, we are dedicated to helping our patients maintain good digestive health. And we strive to
make it as easy and convenient as possible for you.

We combine state-of-the-art medicine with cutting-edge technology (typically seen at elite
hospitals). We provide some of the highest-level care for gastrointestinal, liver disease and
colorectal cancer prevention, detection and screening in the Union County area. At the same time, we
stay committed to providing professional, personal and compassionate care while obtaining complete
patient satisfaction and comfort during the patient’s visit.

Procedures Conditions & Diseases Other GI Care
[

##### Colonoscopy

A colonoscopy is now the gold standard used to detect or prevent individuals from getting colon
cancer. Adults starting at age 45 years are strongly recommended to have a colonoscopy or some other
test to screen for colon cancer.

][19]
[

##### Capsule Endoscopy

During the procedure, a patient swallows a vitamin-sized pill with a camera inside (pill camera).
Transported smoothly and painlessly through the GI tract by the body’s own natural peristalsis, the
video pill capsule transmits images of different parts of your intestine, such as the small
intestine and the esophagus.

][20]
[

##### Breath Testing, including Lactose, Lactulose, Fructose Testing

A breath test is a non-invasive test that can help diagnose a variety of gastrointestinal disorders
and diseases, such as lactose intolerance, fructose intolerance, Helicobacter Pylori infection of
the stomach, and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.

][21]
[

##### Flexible Sigmoidoscopy

A sigmoidoscopy is an internal exam of the lower part of the large intestine (colon) using a short,
thin, flexible, lighted tube with a camera at the tip. This procedure helps determine the cause of
abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, changes in bowel habits, chronic diarrhea, and other intestinal
problems.

][22]
[

##### Hemorrhoid Treatments

Two of the most common treatments for hemorrhoid removal are hemorrhoid banding, which cuts off
blood flow to the hemorrhoid, and infrared coagulation (IRC) therapy, which uses infrared light to
shrink and shrivel hemorrhoids. The treatment method depends highly upon whether the hemorrhoids are
external (around the anus) or internal (in the rectum).

][23]
[

##### Upper Endoscopy

An endoscopy is a very common and safe procedure that is used to examine the esophagus, stomach, and
upper part of the small intestine, known as the duodenum, to get a closer look at what may be
causing symptoms.

][24]
[

##### Celiac Disease

Celiac disease is an autoimmune disease where a patient’s immune system abnormally responds to the
ingestion of gluten. It is estimated that 1 in 100 people worldwide is affected by celiac disease.
However, up to 2.5 million people in the United States may have celiac disease and not know it, as
the symptoms range from mild to severe.

][25]
[

##### Constipation

Constipation is defined as having a bowel movement fewer than three times per week. With
constipation, stools are usually hard, dry, small in size, and difficult to eliminate. Some people
who are constipated find it painful to have a bowel movement and often experience straining,
bloating, and the sensation of a full bowel.

][26]
[

##### GERD

Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a more serious form of gastroesophageal reflux (GER) which
is common. GER occurs when the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) opens spontaneously, for varying
periods of time, or does not close properly, and stomach contents rise up into the esophagus.

][27]
[

##### Hemorrhoids

Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the anal canal. This common problem can be painful and can be
caused by too much pressure on the veins in the pelvic rectal area. Normally, tissue inside the anus
fills with blood to help control bowel movements, but if you strain or sit on the toilet a long time
to move stool, the increased pressure causes the veins in this tissue to swell and stretch.

][28]
[

##### Inflammatory Bowel Disease + Crohn's Disease & Ulcerative Colitis

Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) encompasses a set of gastrointestinal diseases where parts of the
digestive tract are chronically inflamed by a dysfunctional interaction immune system. Hereditary
factors and an abnormal interaction between microorganisms and the immune system are felt to play a
role.

][29]
[

##### Irritable Bowel Syndrome

It is estimated that 10 to 15 percent of Americans have Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). IBS is a
functional GI disorder that refers to a group of symptoms that affect the digestive tract, often
resulting in abdominal pain, bloating, or cramping. However, some people with IBS have no symptoms
at all.

][30]
[

##### Diet & Nutrition

Nutrition plays a paramount role in gastroenterology as it directly influences the health and
functioning of the digestive system. We have nutritional resources available to help understand the
role adequate nutrition plays in preventing and managing various digestive disorders.

][31]
[

##### Fibroscan

We offer FibroScan in our office, a non-invasive diagnostic device designed to measure the
elasticity of liver tissue and detect fibrosis. A fibroscan allows us the ability to provide a
non-surgical alternative to a traditional liver biopsy. We are able to present the results to
patients in real-time and make treatment plan recommendations

][32]
[

##### Infusion Therapy

Infusion Therapy is a medication used to treat inflammatory bowel disease(IBD), which includes
Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis (UC). It is not a first-line treatment method for IBD but
instead a medication given to patients who haven’t responded to more common IBD treatments. Patients
require infusions approximately three to six times a year, depending on the type of medication.
Infusion Therapy works well at arresting symptoms and reducing disease severity, sometimes putting
IBD into remission.

][33]

blood flow to the hemorrhoid, and infrared coagulation (IRC) therapy, which uses infrared light to
shrink and shrivel hemorrhoids. The treatment method depends highly upon whether the hemorrhoids are
external (around the anus) or internal (in the rectum).

][23]
[

##### Upper Endoscopy

An endoscopy is a very common and safe procedure that is used to examine the esophagus, stomach, and
upper part of the small intestine, known as the duodenum, to get a closer look at what may be
causing symptoms.

][24]

##### Celiac Disease

Celiac disease is an autoimmune disease where a patient’s immune system abnormally responds to the
ingestion of gluten. It is estimated that 1 in 100 people worldwide is affected by celiac disease.
However, up to 2.5 million people in the United States may have celiac disease and not know it, as
the symptoms range from mild to severe.

][25]

Constipation is defined as having a bowel movement fewer than three times per week. With
constipation, stools are usually hard, dry, small in size, and difficult to eliminate. Some people
who are constipated find it painful to have a bowel movement and often experience straining,
bloating, and the sensation of a full bowel.

][26]

Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a more serious form of gastroesophageal reflux (GER) which
is common. GER occurs when the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) opens spontaneously, for varying
periods of time, or does not close properly, and stomach contents rise up into the esophagus.

][27]

## About Continuum Gastroenterology Care

Located in the heart of Union County, we combine state-of-the-art technology with gentle care to
provide patients with the best digestive health and endoscopy services possible. We understand that
you need experienced gastroenterologist(s) you can trust. As leading gastroenterologists in Union
County, we are dedicated to helping our patients maintain good digestive health. And we strive to
make it as easy and convenient as possible for you.

We combine state-of-the-art medicine with cutting-edge technology (typically seen at elite
hospitals). We provide some of the highest-level care for gastrointestinal, liver disease and
colorectal cancer prevention, detection and screening in the Union County area. At the same time, we
stay committed to providing professional, personal and compassionate care while obtaining complete
patient satisfaction and comfort during the patient’s visit.

##### Colonoscopy

A colonoscopy is now the gold standard used to detect or prevent individuals from getting colon
cancer. Adults starting at age 45 years are strongly recommended to have a colonoscopy or some other
test to screen for colon cancer.

][19]
[

##### Capsule Endoscopy

During the procedure, a patient swallows a vitamin-sized pill with a camera inside (pill camera).
Transported smoothly and painlessly through the GI tract by the body’s own natural peristalsis, the
video pill capsule transmits images of different parts of your intestine, such as the small
intestine and the esophagus.

][20]
[

##### Breath Testing, including Lactose, Lactulose, Fructose Testing

A breath test is a non-invasive test that can help diagnose a variety of gastrointestinal disorders
and diseases, such as lactose intolerance, fructose intolerance, Helicobacter Pylori infection of
the stomach, and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.

][21]
[

##### Flexible Sigmoidoscopy

A sigmoidoscopy is an internal exam of the lower part of the large intestine (colon) using a short,
thin, flexible, lighted tube with a camera at the tip. This procedure helps determine the cause of
abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, changes in bowel habits, chronic diarrhea, and other intestinal
problems.

][22]
[

##### Inflammatory Bowel Disease + Crohn's Disease & Ulcerative Colitis

Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) encompasses a set of gastrointestinal diseases where parts of the
digestive tract are chronically inflamed by a dysfunctional interaction immune system. Hereditary
factors and an abnormal interaction between microorganisms and the immune system are felt to play a
role.

][29]
[

##### Irritable Bowel Syndrome

It is estimated that 10 to 15 percent of Americans have Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). IBS is a
functional GI disorder that refers to a group of symptoms that affect the digestive tract, often
resulting in abdominal pain, bloating, or cramping. However, some people with IBS have no symptoms
at all.

][30]
[

##### Diet & Nutrition

Nutrition plays a paramount role in gastroenterology as it directly influences the health and
functioning of the digestive system. We have nutritional resources available to help understand the
role adequate nutrition plays in preventing and managing various digestive disorders.

][31]
[

##### Fibroscan

We offer FibroScan in our office, a non-invasive diagnostic device designed to measure the
elasticity of liver tissue and detect fibrosis. A fibroscan allows us the ability to provide a
non-surgical alternative to a traditional liver biopsy. We are able to present the results to
patients in real-time and make treatment plan recommendations

][32]
[

##### Infusion Therapy

Infusion Therapy is a medication used to treat inflammatory bowel disease(IBD), which includes
Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis (UC). It is not a first-line treatment method for IBD but
instead a medication given to patients who haven’t responded to more common IBD treatments. Patients
require infusions approximately three to six times a year, depending on the type of medication.
Infusion Therapy works well at arresting symptoms and reducing disease severity, sometimes putting
IBD into remission.

## Our editorial process

Our mission at DermNet is to provide authoritative skin information for free and we have a strong
process in place to ensure that happens.
* Inclusion
* Comprehensive yet easy to understand
* Free from bias
* Reviewed by Dermatologists
* Up-to-date

[Read more about our editorial process][98]

  childhood. Although many of these are benign and self-limited, some require an extensive workup

## Email Finder FAQ

If you can't find the answer to your question here, visit the dedicated section in our Help Center.

[Visit Help Center][32]

### How should I use the Email Finder?

You may use this search email address tool to find company email addresses, get prospects' valid
emails and other data about them, both on the platform's web app via Search and Enrich and on
LinkedIn via our Email Finder extension (data can also be searched on prospective companies'
websites).

### What data should I upload to find an email address?

To find an email for a prospect, the following data in our web app set is required: first name, last
name, and the company name of the domain (which can be selected from 17 filters). Based on this
information, GetProspect will provide the email address and other prospect data.

### Is it ethical to use an Email Finder?

If you scrape the email addresses for legitimate purposes, such as sales or job hunting, and they
are collected and used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, it may be considered
ethical. But, if you extract emails for sending spam, phishing, or any other illegal purpose, then
it’s unethical.

### Where does GetProspect find emails?

GetProspect Email finder uses its powerful database of over 200 million business contacts with
emails and 26 million companies to find email addresses, as well as LinkedIn's largest and most
current business contacts database with over 900 million users.

### How accurate is the Email Finder?

The accuracy of valid emails that were found on the platform is 95%.

According to the latest tests, GetProspect Email Finder found 84 valid email addresses out of 100
contacts, which is higher than in such alternatives as ZoomInfo, Hunter.io, Lusha, ContactOut, and
others.

### How can I extract an email address from a website?

## Email Finder FAQ

If you can't find the answer to your question here, visit the dedicated section in our Help Center.

[Visit Help Center][32]

### How should I use the Email Finder?

You may use this search email address tool to find company email addresses, get prospects' valid
emails and other data about them, both on the platform's web app via Search and Enrich and on
LinkedIn via our Email Finder extension (data can also be searched on prospective companies'
websites).

### What data should I upload to find an email address?

To find an email for a prospect, the following data in our web app set is required: first name, last
name, and the company name of the domain (which can be selected from 17 filters). Based on this
information, GetProspect will provide the email address and other prospect data.

### Is it ethical to use an Email Finder?

If you scrape the email addresses for legitimate purposes, such as sales or job hunting, and they
are collected and used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, it may be considered
ethical. But, if you extract emails for sending spam, phishing, or any other illegal purpose, then
it’s unethical.

### Where does GetProspect find emails?

GetProspect Email finder uses its powerful database of over 200 million business contacts with
emails and 26 million companies to find email addresses, as well as LinkedIn's largest and most
current business contacts database with over 900 million users.

### How accurate is the Email Finder?

The accuracy of valid emails that were found on the platform is 95%.

According to the latest tests, GetProspect Email Finder found 84 valid email addresses out of 100
contacts, which is higher than in such alternatives as ZoomInfo, Hunter.io, Lusha, ContactOut, and
others.

### How can I extract an email address from a website?

Once the extension is installed, it can be used for fetching basic info about the companies,

# [Interplay of Genetics and Pediatric Pancreatitis][8]

Posted on [July 24, 2026][9] by [gutsandgrowth][10]
[Reply][11]

**M Abu-El-Haija et al. Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, 2026. (Article in print). DOI:
10.1016/j.cgh.2026.06.004**. Open Access! [Pancreatitis Risk Genes Play a Major Role in Pediatric
Pancreatitis: Insights From INSPPIRE][12]

**Methods: **A cross-sectional study involving 944 pediatric ARP or CP subjects was
conducted. *CASR, CEL, CFTR, CLDN2, CPA1, CTRC, GGT1, PRSS1, PRSS2, PRSS3, SBDS, SLC26A9,
SPINK1,* and *UBR1* were sequenced.

**Key findings: **
* A total of 120 variants, including 79 never previously reported to be associated with
  pancreatitis.
* 38 focused variants found in CFTR (10 variants), PRSS1 (6), CTRC (6), SPINK1 (5), PRSS3 (3), GGT1
  (3), CASR (2), CPA1 (2), and PRSS2 (1).
* Seventy-four percent of children with acute recurrent pancreatitis (ARP) and chronic pancreatitis
  (CP) carried at least one genetic risk variant.
* In CP, *CTRC* (p=0.012) and *PRSS1* (p<0.001) variants were most common. The presence of any
  genetic risk variant was associated with faster disease progression from AP to CP compared to none
  (p=0.014).

**My take**: This study shows the essential role that genetic mutations have in increasing the risk
of ARP or CP. It reinforces the need for genettic testing in children with more than one episode of
acute pancreatitis.

# [Endoscopic Ischemic Polypectomy for Polyposis Disorders][26]

Posted on [July 23, 2026][27] by [gutsandgrowth][28]
[Reply][29]

**S Kurasawa et al. JPGN Reports. 2026; DOI: 10.1002/jpr3.70188.** Open Access! [Endoscopic ischemic
polypectomy for small intestinal polyps in a 7-year-old girl with juvenile polyposis syndrome][30]

**Background: **“Funayama et al.^{[4][31]} described the technique of endoscopic ischemic
polypectomy (EIP) in detail in both pediatric and adult patients with Peutz–Jeghers syndrome (PJS).
Subsequently, EIP was reported to be a safe and effective treatment for 269 small intestinal polyps
in 22 pediatric PJS cases.^{[5][32]}” Here the authors describe the use of this technique for a
child with juvenile polyposis syndrome (JPS).

**Key findings:**
* During a two-hour double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) for a 7 yo child, “17 pedunculated polyps, all
  with a visually assessed size range of 7–15 mm, EIP was performed using the “crossed-clip
  strangulation method,” in which the first hemostatic clip was deployed with the aid of a distal
  attachment and rotated 90°, followed by placement of a second clip crossing the first at a 90°
  angle (Figure [1][33])…Subsequently, anemia and hypoalbuminemia did not recur, and growth was
  satisfied.”

(A) Pedunculated polyp in the small intestine. (B) The first hemostatic clip was placed on the stalk
of the polyp. (C) A second hemostatic clip was placed on the stalk of the polyp at a 90-degree angle
to the first clip.

**Discussion Points:**
* “EIP does not involve electrocautery, eliminating the risk of thermal injury and offering a safer
  alternative for small bowel lesions.”
* “A limitation of EIP is the inability to retrieve resected polyps…It should only be used for
  lesions that appear clearly benign.”
* There is a risk of detached polyps migrating into the lower gastrointestinal tract and inducing
  intussusception. This can be mitigated by managing distal small intestinal polyps first.

**My take**: EIP appears to be useful for inidividuals with numerous small intestinal polyps.

# [Dupilumab for Eosinophilic Gastritis: DEGAS study][60]

Posted on [July 22, 2026][61] by [gutsandgrowth][62]
[Reply][63]

**N Gonsalves, E Dellon E, K Kliewer K et al. The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 2026;**
DOI: [10.1016/S2468-1253(26)00116-0][64]. Open Access! [Dupilumab versus placebo in adults and
adolescents with eosinophilic gastritis (DEGAS): a double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2,
multicentre, randomised controlled trial][65]

**Methods: **This was a phase 2b trial with a 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled period,
followed by a 24-week open-label extension period. Patients aged 12–70 years from 11 hospitals in
the USA with histologically active eosinophilic gastritis (≥30 eosinophils per high-power field
[HPF] in at least five HPFs in the gastric antrum and/or body) and moderate-to-severe symptoms.
Eligible patients were individually randomised (1:1) to parallel groups and received six injections
over 12 weeks: subcutaneous dupilumab (n=21) (600 mg once followed by 300 mg every 2 weeks) or
subcutaneous placebo (n=20).  The primary endpoint of relative change from baseline in mean gastric
eosinophil count.

**Key findings: **
* At week 12, the relative reduction in the primary endpoint was greater with dupilumab (estimated
  mean change –50%) than with placebo (–4%)
* Reduction from baseline in EoG-REFS (Eosinophilic Gastritis Endoscopic Reference Score) at week 12
  was greater with dupilumab (estimated mean change –3·47 points than with placebo (–0·06 points)

 

 

**Discussion Points:**

“Currently, there are no FDA-approved therapies for patients with eosinophilic gastritis…this first
prospective trial of dupilumab for eosinophilic gastritis show a greater reduction in mean gastric
eosinophil count from the five most eosinophil-dense HPFs (the primary endpoint) with dupilumab
compared with placebo.”

**My take: **Dupilumab improved eosinophilic gastritis histology and endoscopic appearance. This
study suggests that there may be overlapping pathophysiology between eosinophilic gastritis and
eosinophilic esophagits as dupilumab appers to be effective in both disorders.

# [How Effective is Ustekinumab Dose Intensification in Crohn’s Disease: REScUE Trial][77]

Posted on [July 21, 2026][78] by [gutsandgrowth][79]
[Reply][80]
* **P Bossuyt et al. Gastroenterol 2026; 171: 99-109**. Open Access! [The Effect of Dose
  Intensification After Secondary Loss of Response to Ustekinumab in Crohn’s Disease: Results of the
  REScUE Study][81]
* **J Burisch.** **Gastroenterol 2026; 171: 24-25** (editorial). Open Access! [Reinduction or
  Redirection? Lessons From the REScUE Trial on Ustekinumab Intensification in Crohn’s Disease][82]

**Methods:** This was an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
conducted at 15 hospitals in Belgium. Eligible patients were adults (n=108) with CD treated with
ustekinumab on maintenance dosing of 90 mg subcutaneous every 8 weeks and experiencing a secondary
loss of response. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receiving a single intravenous reinduction with
ustekinumab ≈6 mg/kg followed by either subcutaneous ustekinumab 90 mg every 4 weeks or every 8
weeks until week 48. 

**Key findings:**
* Steroid-free clinical remission at week 48 was reached in 15% vs 19% of patients in the every 4
  weeks vs the every 8 weeks group 

**Discussion Points:**
* “Remarkably, the overall steroid-free clinical remission rates at week 48 were low in both arms:
  15% and 19% for ustekinumab Q4W and Q8W, respectively. Most of the patients achieved clinical
  remission in the first 24 weeks after IV reinduction though, suggesting that the IV reinduction is
  the main driver of the effectiveness, rather than the subsequent SC dose intensification.”
* “Our results are in contrast with several retrospective and observational nonrandomized and
  open-label cohort studies suggesting a clinical response rate after dose intensification up to 60%
  and clinical remission rates up to 50% after 1 year of treatment.[⁴][83]^{,}[^{13–17}][84]“

The associated editorial notes that the modest remission rate could be partly due to a more
refractory patient poulation. “The cohort was indeed difficult to treat: median disease duration
exceeded a decade, and more than 90% of patients had prior anti–tumor necrosis factor exposure.”
Despite this caveat, “the trial avoids overestimating therapeutic success and aligns outcomes with
contemporary treat-to-target principles.[⁴][85] From this perspective, REScUE provides a realistic
benchmark for what ustekinumab intensification can and cannot achieve in routine clinical practice.”

The editorial also notes that the “STARDUST trial [which] evaluated a treat-to-target,
endoscopy-guided escalation algorithm vs standard of care in ustekinumab-treated CD and did not
demonstrate a clear advantage for the intensive, endoscopy-driven strategy at 1 year.[⁷][86]“

**My take **(borrowed from editorial): “In carefully selected patients who previously responded well
to ustekinumab, a short and closely monitored trial of IV reinduction may be considered. However,
the threshold for switching to another advanced therapy should remain low if treatment targets are
not achieved.”

# [Interplay of Genetics and Pediatric Pancreatitis][8]

Posted on [July 24, 2026][9] by [gutsandgrowth][10]
[Reply][11]

**M Abu-El-Haija et al. Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, 2026. (Article in print). DOI:
10.1016/j.cgh.2026.06.004**. Open Access! [Pancreatitis Risk Genes Play a Major Role in Pediatric
Pancreatitis: Insights From INSPPIRE][12]

**Methods: **A cross-sectional study involving 944 pediatric ARP or CP subjects was
conducted. *CASR, CEL, CFTR, CLDN2, CPA1, CTRC, GGT1, PRSS1, PRSS2, PRSS3, SBDS, SLC26A9,
SPINK1,* and *UBR1* were sequenced.

**Key findings: **
* A total of 120 variants, including 79 never previously reported to be associated with
  pancreatitis.
* 38 focused variants found in CFTR (10 variants), PRSS1 (6), CTRC (6), SPINK1 (5), PRSS3 (3), GGT1
  (3), CASR (2), CPA1 (2), and PRSS2 (1).
* Seventy-four percent of children with acute recurrent pancreatitis (ARP) and chronic pancreatitis
  (CP) carried at least one genetic risk variant.
* In CP, *CTRC* (p=0.012) and *PRSS1* (p<0.001) variants were most common. The presence of any
  genetic risk variant was associated with faster disease progression from AP to CP compared to none
  (p=0.014).

**My take**: This study shows the essential role that genetic mutations have in increasing the risk
of ARP or CP. It reinforces the need for genettic testing in children with more than one episode of
acute pancreatitis.

# [Endoscopic Ischemic Polypectomy for Polyposis Disorders][26]

Posted on [July 23, 2026][27] by [gutsandgrowth][28]
[Reply][29]

**S Kurasawa et al. JPGN Reports. 2026; DOI: 10.1002/jpr3.70188.** Open Access! [Endoscopic ischemic
polypectomy for small intestinal polyps in a 7-year-old girl with juvenile polyposis syndrome][30]

**Background: **“Funayama et al.^{[4][31]} described the technique of endoscopic ischemic
polypectomy (EIP) in detail in both pediatric and adult patients with Peutz–Jeghers syndrome (PJS).
Subsequently, EIP was reported to be a safe and effective treatment for 269 small intestinal polyps
in 22 pediatric PJS cases.^{[5][32]}” Here the authors describe the use of this technique for a
child with juvenile polyposis syndrome (JPS).

**Key findings:**
* During a two-hour double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) for a 7 yo child, “17 pedunculated polyps, all
  with a visually assessed size range of 7–15 mm, EIP was performed using the “crossed-clip
  strangulation method,” in which the first hemostatic clip was deployed with the aid of a distal
  attachment and rotated 90°, followed by placement of a second clip crossing the first at a 90°
  angle (Figure [1][33])…Subsequently, anemia and hypoalbuminemia did not recur, and growth was
  satisfied.”

(A) Pedunculated polyp in the small intestine. (B) The first hemostatic clip was placed on the stalk
of the polyp. (C) A second hemostatic clip was placed on the stalk of the polyp at a 90-degree angle
to the first clip.

**Discussion Points:**
* “EIP does not involve electrocautery, eliminating the risk of thermal injury and offering a safer
  alternative for small bowel lesions.”
* “A limitation of EIP is the inability to retrieve resected polyps…It should only be used for
  lesions that appear clearly benign.”
* There is a risk of detached polyps migrating into the lower gastrointestinal tract and inducing
  intussusception. This can be mitigated by managing distal small intestinal polyps first.

**My take**: EIP appears to be useful for inidividuals with numerous small intestinal polyps.

# [Dupilumab for Eosinophilic Gastritis: DEGAS study][60]

Posted on [July 22, 2026][61] by [gutsandgrowth][62]
[Reply][63]

**N Gonsalves, E Dellon E, K Kliewer K et al. The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 2026;**
DOI: [10.1016/S2468-1253(26)00116-0][64]. Open Access! [Dupilumab versus placebo in adults and
adolescents with eosinophilic gastritis (DEGAS): a double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2,
multicentre, randomised controlled trial][65]

**Methods: **This was a phase 2b trial with a 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled period,
followed by a 24-week open-label extension period. Patients aged 12–70 years from 11 hospitals in
the USA with histologically active eosinophilic gastritis (≥30 eosinophils per high-power field
[HPF] in at least five HPFs in the gastric antrum and/or body) and moderate-to-severe symptoms.
Eligible patients were individually randomised (1:1) to parallel groups and received six injections
over 12 weeks: subcutaneous dupilumab (n=21) (600 mg once followed by 300 mg every 2 weeks) or
subcutaneous placebo (n=20).  The primary endpoint of relative change from baseline in mean gastric
eosinophil count.

**Key findings: **
* At week 12, the relative reduction in the primary endpoint was greater with dupilumab (estimated
  mean change –50%) than with placebo (–4%)
* Reduction from baseline in EoG-REFS (Eosinophilic Gastritis Endoscopic Reference Score) at week 12
  was greater with dupilumab (estimated mean change –3·47 points than with placebo (–0·06 points)

 

 

**Discussion Points:**

“Currently, there are no FDA-approved therapies for patients with eosinophilic gastritis…this first
prospective trial of dupilumab for eosinophilic gastritis show a greater reduction in mean gastric
eosinophil count from the five most eosinophil-dense HPFs (the primary endpoint) with dupilumab
compared with placebo.”

**My take: **Dupilumab improved eosinophilic gastritis histology and endoscopic appearance. This
study suggests that there may be overlapping pathophysiology between eosinophilic gastritis and
eosinophilic esophagits as dupilumab appers to be effective in both disorders.

# [How Effective is Ustekinumab Dose Intensification in Crohn’s Disease: REScUE Trial][77]

Posted on [July 21, 2026][78] by [gutsandgrowth][79]
[Reply][80]
* **P Bossuyt et al. Gastroenterol 2026; 171: 99-109**. Open Access! [The Effect of Dose
  Intensification After Secondary Loss of Response to Ustekinumab in Crohn’s Disease: Results of the
  REScUE Study][81]
* **J Burisch.** **Gastroenterol 2026; 171: 24-25** (editorial). Open Access! [Reinduction or
  Redirection? Lessons From the REScUE Trial on Ustekinumab Intensification in Crohn’s Disease][82]

**Methods:** This was an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
conducted at 15 hospitals in Belgium. Eligible patients were adults (n=108) with CD treated with
ustekinumab on maintenance dosing of 90 mg subcutaneous every 8 weeks and experiencing a secondary
loss of response. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receiving a single intravenous reinduction with
ustekinumab ≈6 mg/kg followed by either subcutaneous ustekinumab 90 mg every 4 weeks or every 8
weeks until week 48. 

**Key findings:**
* Steroid-free clinical remission at week 48 was reached in 15% vs 19% of patients in the every 4
  weeks vs the every 8 weeks group 

**Discussion Points:**
* “Remarkably, the overall steroid-free clinical remission rates at week 48 were low in both arms:
  15% and 19% for ustekinumab Q4W and Q8W, respectively. Most of the patients achieved clinical
  remission in the first 24 weeks after IV reinduction though, suggesting that the IV reinduction is
  the main driver of the effectiveness, rather than the subsequent SC dose intensification.”
* “Our results are in contrast with several retrospective and observational nonrandomized and
  open-label cohort studies suggesting a clinical response rate after dose intensification up to 60%
  and clinical remission rates up to 50% after 1 year of treatment.[⁴][83]^{,}[^{13–17}][84]“

The associated editorial notes that the modest remission rate could be partly due to a more
refractory patient poulation. “The cohort was indeed difficult to treat: median disease duration
exceeded a decade, and more than 90% of patients had prior anti–tumor necrosis factor exposure.”
Despite this caveat, “the trial avoids overestimating therapeutic success and aligns outcomes with
contemporary treat-to-target principles.[⁴][85] From this perspective, REScUE provides a realistic
benchmark for what ustekinumab intensification can and cannot achieve in routine clinical practice.”

The editorial also notes that the “STARDUST trial [which] evaluated a treat-to-target,
endoscopy-guided escalation algorithm vs standard of care in ustekinumab-treated CD and did not
demonstrate a clear advantage for the intensive, endoscopy-driven strategy at 1 year.[⁷][86]“

**My take **(borrowed from editorial): “In carefully selected patients who previously responded well
to ustekinumab, a short and closely monitored trial of IV reinduction may be considered. However,
the threshold for switching to another advanced therapy should remain low if treatment targets are
not achieved.”

## Frequently asked questions

#### How much does a doctor visit with HealthTap cost?

With insurance, you pay your copay based on your plan. We accept most plans, including Medicare.

Without insurance, online doctor visits are $129. You can become a HealthTap member and pay
$44/visit. Membership is $55 for three months and $180 for a yearly membership.

#### Do you accept health insurance?

Yes! We accept all major insurance plans—including Medicare Advantage and traditional Medicare. We
also accept HSA and FSA cards.

#### Do you accept Medicare?

Yes! We accept traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans. The price of the visit will be
your copay.

#### How much would an online doctor visit cost if I don't have insurance or if my deductible is
#### very high?

Without insurance, online doctor visits are $129. You can become a HealthTap member and pay
$44/visit. Membership is $55 for three months and $180 for a yearly membership.

#### Can I pay with my HSA and FSA card?

Yes, we accept HSA and FSA cards.

#### What is HealthTap membership and how much does it cost?

Membership is $55 for three months and $180 for a yearly membership. Members get unlimited texting
with their doctors, $44 primary care visits, $59 urgent care visits, and more.

#### What kind of technology or software do I need for an online doctor visit?

You can join with any device that has a stable internet connection—including your phone, tablet, or
laptop.

#### How can a HealthTap doctor help me?

Our primary care doctors are available for checkups, sudden illness, chronic conditions,
prescription refills, and more. They're here to listen and be a partner in your health journey for
years to come.

#### Does HealthTap give doctor's notes?

Yes. HealthTap doctors can provide notes to verify that you've seen a doctor about your overall
health or for a specific medical condition. These can be used for participation in sports programs,
for school programs, or given to your employer.

#### Are there any medications that HealthTap doctors cannot prescribe?

There are some medications that are always prescribed in-person and cannot be prescribed by
HealthTap doctors (or any other doctor seeing a patient online). These include opioids and other
controlled substances and some psychiatric and lifestyle drugs.

#### What credentials do HealthTap doctors have?

HealthTap doctors who conduct online doctor visits are based in the U.S. and have at least one
medical degree. Additionally, they are board-certified with an accredited American Board of Medical
Specialities (ABMS) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA) speciality board. They have a valid
and unrestricted license to practice in one or more U.S. states and no significant adverse
professional action against the doctor's medical license.

#### Should I download the HealthTap mobile app?

If you plan to use HealthTap on your smartphone or tablet, the HealthTap app makes it even easier to
take advantage of our features, including scheduling and conducting online doctor visits.

## Have a health question?

Create a free HealthTap account and ask any health question to our 90K+ doctors. No topic is too
embarrassing — it's 100% confidential. Most questions are answered the same day.

controlled substances and some psychiatric and lifestyle drugs.

#### What credentials do HealthTap doctors have?

HealthTap doctors who conduct online doctor visits are based in the U.S. and have at least one
medical degree. Additionally, they are board-certified with an accredited American Board of Medical
Specialities (ABMS) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA) speciality board. They have a valid
and unrestricted license to practice in one or more U.S. states and no significant adverse
professional action against the doctor's medical license.

#### Should I download the HealthTap mobile app?

If you plan to use HealthTap on your smartphone or tablet, the HealthTap app makes it even easier to
take advantage of our features, including scheduling and conducting online doctor visits.

## Have a health question?

Create a free HealthTap account and ask any health question to our 90K+ doctors. No topic is too
embarrassing — it's 100% confidential. Most questions are answered the same day.

# Гепцифол^{®} — гепатопротектор с адеметионином

Аминокислота естественного происхождения

Адеметионин выполняет ключевую роль в метаболических процессах организма. Способствует улучшению
и поддержанию функций печени, снижению утомляемости при установленных хронических заболеваниях.

## Эффекты Гепцифола®

[Печень] Механизм действия
* Помощь в восстановлении структуры клеток
  
  Способствует прекращению процессов разрушения гепатоцитов и запуску механизма восстановления на
  клеточном уровне¹
* Детоксикационное действие
  
  Может помочь в обезвреживании многих продуктов обмена веществ и восстановлении поврежденных
  тканевых структур^{2,3}
* Регенерирующее свойство
  
  Адеметионин способствует окислительно-восстановительному механизму клеточного «очищения»¹
* Нейропротективное действие
  
  Оказывает действие, направленное на защиту клеток нервной системы от повреждающих воздействий и
  предотвращение их гибели, тем самым способствует улучшению психоэмоционального фона¹
[Больше о препарате ][17]

## Особенности применения

Время наступления действия препарата⁴

Эффект от приема Гепцифола
обычно проявляется через
7-14 дней лечения⁵

Оптимальный курс

Возможен прием 1 раз в день⁵, рекомендуемый курс приема препарата от 1 месяца^{5,6}

Пролонгированное действие

Гепатопротекторное действие может сохраняться до 3 месяцев после прекращения лечения⁵

Гепцифол оказался удобным – вся доза за раз, без сложных схем. Спустя несколько дней заметила, что
тяжесть исчезла, самочувствие стало лучше. По сравнению с аналогами, курс короче, что удобно.

SokolEk 009.рф

+7 (928) *** ** 88 apteka-april.ru

10.03.2025 [Посмотреть отзыв ][37]

# Гепцифол^{®} — гепатопротектор с адеметионином

Аминокислота естественного происхождения

Адеметионин выполняет ключевую роль в метаболических процессах организма. Способствует улучшению
и поддержанию функций печени, снижению утомляемости при установленных хронических заболеваниях.

## Эффекты Гепцифола®

[Печень] Механизм действия
* Помощь в восстановлении структуры клеток
  
  Способствует прекращению процессов разрушения гепатоцитов и запуску механизма восстановления на
  клеточном уровне¹
* Детоксикационное действие
  
  Может помочь в обезвреживании многих продуктов обмена веществ и восстановлении поврежденных
  тканевых структур^{2,3}
* Регенерирующее свойство
  
  Адеметионин способствует окислительно-восстановительному механизму клеточного «очищения»¹
* Нейропротективное действие
  
  Оказывает действие, направленное на защиту клеток нервной системы от повреждающих воздействий и
  предотвращение их гибели, тем самым способствует улучшению психоэмоционального фона¹

# Гепцифол^{®} — гепатопротектор с адеметионином

Аминокислота естественного происхождения

Адеметионин выполняет ключевую роль в метаболических процессах организма. Способствует улучшению
и поддержанию функций печени, снижению утомляемости при установленных хронических заболеваниях.

## Эффекты Гепцифола®

[Печень] Механизм действия
* Помощь в восстановлении структуры клеток
  
  Способствует прекращению процессов разрушения гепатоцитов и запуску механизма восстановления на
  клеточном уровне¹
* Детоксикационное действие
  
  Может помочь в обезвреживании многих продуктов обмена веществ и восстановлении поврежденных
  тканевых структур^{2,3}
* Регенерирующее свойство
  
  Адеметионин способствует окислительно-восстановительному механизму клеточного «очищения»¹
* Нейропротективное действие
  
  Оказывает действие, направленное на защиту клеток нервной системы от повреждающих воздействий и
  предотвращение их гибели, тем самым способствует улучшению психоэмоционального фона¹

are cost effective.

06/11/2026

Manufacturer setting a price for oveporexton to align with value would help promote broad patient

## Our Origin Story.

Dr. Steve Pearson explains why he founded an organization to advance the use of evidence to improve
health care affordability and access for all patients and their families.

## The ICER Impact.

New York Medicaid pursued discounts, many of which were in line with ICER reports, which have saved
the state over $500 million

**[Read More][41]**

## Engaged with over 400 patient groups and patient reps

The ICER-developed Clinical trial Diversity Rating (CDR) Tool presents a framework for evaluating
the demographic diversity of clinical trial populations in a consistent, transparent manner leading
to an overall diversity rating.** [Learn more][42].**

 

[Learn More About ICER’s Impact][43]

## Current

## Policy Papers.

Easy access to our latest policy papers

### [Strengthening the FDA’s Accelerated Approval Pathway: Progress and Unfinished Business][44]

ICER, in collaboration with Verdant Research, will publish a new white paper that examines the
evolution – and perception – of the FDA accelerated approval pathway. The paper, entitled,
“Strengthening the FDA’s Accelerated Approval Pathway: Progress and Unfinished Business,” will
review recent regulatory and market changes and propose several policy options that focuses on
improvements that could be made by regulators, payers and manufacturers.

[Read More][45]

### [Launch Price and Access Report: Drug Approvals from 2022-2024][46]

ICER conducted a new analysis it plans to release on an annual basis titled the “Launch Price and
Access Report” which examines launch pricing for FDA-approved treatments. This report reviewed the
affordability and access of the treatments and their value to the overall health system.

[Read More][47]

### [Special Assessment to Inform CMS Drug Price Negotiation: Vedolizumab (Entyvio®)][48]

ICER is developed a special report for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services on a therapy for
treating Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. This report was submitted to CMS as part of the
2026 public comment process defined in CMS guidance on Medicare Drug Price Negotiations for price
applicability year 2028.

[Read More][49]

# Highly Validated Approaches to Highly Unmet Needs.

## Developing Treatments for Severe Liver Disease.

## about

Inipharm is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing
therapies for severe liver diseases. Inipharm's lead program is focused on the highly validated,
genetically-defined target, HSD17B13.

Inipharm, through its Australian subsidiary Inipharm Australia, Pty Ltd, is conducting a Phase 1
clinical trial, including MASH patients, of INI-822, a first in class small molecule inhibitor of
HSD17B13.

There is extensive, consistent evidence that genetic variants of HSD17B13 are associated with
significantly lower rates and severity of multiple liver diseases. Building on these novel insights
into the biologic activity of HSD17B13, Inipharm is advancing a pipeline of small-molecule therapies
that target the activity of this protein.

## clinical development

### First clinical-stage small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13

Inipharm, through its Australian subsidiary Inipharm Australia, Pty Ltd, is conducting clinical
development of INI-822, the first small molecule HSD inhibitor. Phase 1 work in healthy volunteers
has been completed and testing in patients with MASH is underway. For more information:

#### Clinical pharmacokinetics of INI-822, a small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13

[[Clinical pharmacokinetics of INI-822, a small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13]Click here to
download PDF][7]

## our science

Inipharm is developing small-molecule inhibitors of HSD17B13 to treat fibrotic liver diseases.
Inipharm's inhibitors have been shown to drive alterations in lipid metabolism and improvements in
liver enzymes that are consistent with changes seen with the protective variant in humans. In human
liver cell-based systems, INI-822 demonstrated anti-fibrotic effects.

Protective variants in HSD17B13 are associated with reduced risk incidence and/or the severity of
numerous liver diseases.
* HSD17B13 has been identified as a novel target for NASH and driver of liver disease from a genome
  wide association study.
* Loss of function variants in HSD17B13 are associated with reduced risk incidence and/or the
  severity of numerous liver diseases.
* Importantly, HSD17B13 has been shown to be involved in pathways associated with lipotoxicity,
  inflammation, and fibrosis.

[HSD17B13 Disease Association Chart]SOURCES: Gellert-Kristensen 2019; Abul-Husn 2018; Kozlitina
2018; About 2018; Ferenci 2019, Yang 2020 Hepatol; About 2018 NEJM

### INI-822, development candidate
* Reduced fibrotic markers in human liver cell model
* Improved liver enzymes in multiple in vivo models
* Replicated lipidomic changes seen with protective HSD17B13 variant

[[HSD17B13 Disease Association Chart]Click here to download PDF][8]

#### phosphatidylcholines in a diet-dependent manner

phosphatidylcholines in a diet-dependent manner]Click here to download PDF][9]

# Highly Validated Approaches to Highly Unmet Needs.

## Developing Treatments for Severe Liver Disease.

## about

Inipharm is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing
therapies for severe liver diseases. Inipharm's lead program is focused on the highly validated,
genetically-defined target, HSD17B13.

Inipharm, through its Australian subsidiary Inipharm Australia, Pty Ltd, is conducting a Phase 1
clinical trial, including MASH patients, of INI-822, a first in class small molecule inhibitor of
HSD17B13.

There is extensive, consistent evidence that genetic variants of HSD17B13 are associated with
significantly lower rates and severity of multiple liver diseases. Building on these novel insights
into the biologic activity of HSD17B13, Inipharm is advancing a pipeline of small-molecule therapies
that target the activity of this protein.

## clinical development

### First clinical-stage small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13

Inipharm, through its Australian subsidiary Inipharm Australia, Pty Ltd, is conducting clinical
development of INI-822, the first small molecule HSD inhibitor. Phase 1 work in healthy volunteers
has been completed and testing in patients with MASH is underway. For more information:

#### Clinical pharmacokinetics of INI-822, a small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13

[[Clinical pharmacokinetics of INI-822, a small molecule inhibitor of HSD17B13]Click here to
download PDF][7]

## our science

Inipharm is developing small-molecule inhibitors of HSD17B13 to treat fibrotic liver diseases.
Inipharm's inhibitors have been shown to drive alterations in lipid metabolism and improvements in
liver enzymes that are consistent with changes seen with the protective variant in humans. In human
liver cell-based systems, INI-822 demonstrated anti-fibrotic effects.

Protective variants in HSD17B13 are associated with reduced risk incidence and/or the severity of
numerous liver diseases.
* HSD17B13 has been identified as a novel target for NASH and driver of liver disease from a genome
  wide association study.
* Loss of function variants in HSD17B13 are associated with reduced risk incidence and/or the
  severity of numerous liver diseases.
* Importantly, HSD17B13 has been shown to be involved in pathways associated with lipotoxicity,
  inflammation, and fibrosis.

#### Detailed Market Analysis

The pharmaceutical industry is undergoing a remarkable digital transformation, supported by concrete
market research and verified statistics. The scale of this transformation is evidenced by the
pharmaceutical digital platform market’s projected growth from $4.92 billion in 2023 to $34.12
billion by 2032, representing a robust CAGR of 24.35%. This growth is driven by widespread cloud
adoption, with approximately 80% of pharmaceutical companies already utilizing cloud computing
solutions and 95% expected to be fully cloud-operational within two years.

The transformation is happening across multiple dimensions, with web-based solutions dominating at
72.27% market share and AI-driven engagement representing 27.05% of patient engagement solutions.
Quality management systems are also evolving, with the market expected to grow from $1.87 billion in
2024 to $3.85 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 12.99%. This digital evolution is particularly strong in
North America, which holds a 43.6% share in patient engagement solutions and 39% of the quality
management software market. Implementation timelines vary by solution complexity, ranging from 3-6
months for modular SaaS deployments to 9-18 months for full-suite implementations, reflecting the
industry’s methodical approach to digital adoption while maintaining compliance with regulatory
requirements.
